ns_chimney_calm.name: Plume in Calm Air
ns_chimney_calm.question: What does the same source do without wind?

layers.title: The question
layers.text: What does the same source do without wind?

layers.title: What the colours and motion show
layers.text: The same stack and source with no crosswind. The plume rises vertically and meanders only through its own instability.

layers.title: One change to try
items: Compare with the crosswind scenes in the run history.

layers.title: What to measure
layers.text: A near-vertical trajectory in the diagnostics.

layers.title: Physical explanation
layers.text:
A buoyant plume leaves a stack into a steady horizontal wind. Right at the source buoyancy dominates and the hot, dyed fluid shoots almost straight up. But the crosswind never stops pushing, so a little higher the plume bends over and trails away downwind in the familiar slanted smokestack shape.

How high it climbs before levelling off — the 'plume rise' — is a tug-of-war between the buoyancy lifting it and the wind's momentum sweeping it sideways. Strengthen the wind and the plume bends sooner and stays lower; increase the buoyancy and it punches higher first. That balance is exactly what engineers estimate when they size a smokestack and predict how far a pollutant travels before it reaches the ground.

As a rule of thumb the plume rise grows with the source's buoyancy and shrinks as the wind speeds up (the idea behind the Briggs plume-rise formulas used in air-quality models): a tall, buoyant, slow-wind plume stays high and dilutes before it descends, while a strong crosswind bends it down early and brings it to ground sooner. The trajectory plot in the player traces exactly this bend-over.

layers.title: Equations, symbols and assumptions
layers.text:
• (u·∇)u — advection: the mean wind carries the plume downstream
• f_b = αg T ŷ — Boussinesq buoyancy from the hot, dyed source lifts the plume
• ν∇²u — viscous diffusion; ∇·u = 0 — incompressibility (the pressure projection)
• velocity inlet (the wind) on the left, open outflow on the right, open top
• plume rise ∝ buoyancy ÷ wind — the trade-off that sets the bent-over trajectory

layers.title: Initial and boundary conditions (this preset)
layers.ic: A uniform crosswind already blowing across a box of clean air.
layers.bc: Velocity inlet (the wind) on the left, zero-gradient outflow on the right, a no-penetration (free-slip) floor with a hot dyed stack source, open top.

layers.title: Numerical method, checks and limitations
layers.text: The projection solver with a hot, dyed source at the floor and a velocity inlet on the left that drives a uniform crosswind (zero-gradient outflow on the right, open top). Boussinesq buoyancy lifts the dyed fluid while the mean wind advects it downstream, so the steady plume trajectory emerges from the force balance.
layers.checks: Qualitative demonstration (reference case for the wind sweep).

layers.title: References
items: Briggs, G.A. (1975). Plume rise predictions. In: Lectures on Air Pollution and Environmental Impact Analyses, AMS.

buoyancy.label: Buoyancy coefficient
buoyancy.help: Buoyancy coefficient: force per unit of the transported scalar (dye/temperature). Higher → a faster, more vigorous plume.

wind.label: Crosswind speed
wind.help: Speed of the horizontal wind across the stack. Stronger wind bends the plume over closer to the ground (a smaller plume rise). 0 = calm air.

confinement.label: Vorticity confinement
confinement.help: Vorticity confinement — re-injects small-scale swirl lost to numerical diffusion (a modelling knob, not a physical property). 0 = none.

source.label: Stack width
source.help: Width of the chimney source at the floor.

viscosity.label: Viscosity
viscosity.help: Kinematic viscosity ν — how 'thick' the fluid is. Lower → finer, more chaotic structures; higher → smoother, damped flow.

resolution.label: Resolution
resolution.help: Grid resolution. It changes the grid, and with it whatever a scene ties to the grid: the elapsed convective time in the wind tunnel, the Rayleigh number in the convection scenes, the grain size in the rock, the extent of the blast box. The derived readouts say what moved for this experiment; runs at different resolutions are comparable only where they say so.

duration.label: Duration (×)
duration.help: Simulated interval as a multiple of the scene's reference interval (1.0 = default).
